title: TWA 553

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Aircraft Accident Report - Trans World Airlines, Inc., Douglas DC-9, N1063T and Beechcraft Baron, near Urbana, Ohio

summary: Trans World Airlines Flight 553, a McDonnell Douglas DC-9, collided in midair with a Beechcraft Baron piloted privately near Urbana, Ohio on March 9, 1967. The DC-9 was descending at 323 knots through 4,500 feet when its front right side struck the left side of the Baron. Due to the DC-9's high descent rate, its pilots were unable to see the Baron in time to avoid the collision, killing all 26 occupants of both aircraft.
probable_cause: The midair collision was caused by the flight crew of the DC-9 failing to see and avoid the Beechcraft Baron during descent. The DC-9's high rate of descent (estimated at 2,000+ fpm) and the crew's divided attention between descent/approach procedures and traffic surveillance made visual detection of the smaller Beechcraft difficult or impossible within the available reaction time.

factors.evidence: The DC-9 was descending at 323 knots through 4,500 feet when it collided with the Baron. The high descent rate resulted in reduced visibility outside the cockpit for the DC-9 pilots.

The crew of the DC-9 failed to see the Beechcraft Baron despite a traffic advisory issued by Dayton radar approach control approximately 18 seconds before collision. The crew acknowledged the advisory but did not successfully acquire visual contact.
The front right side of the DC-9 collided with the left side of the Beechcraft Baron 55, resulting in the destruction of both aircraft and loss of all 26 occupants.

events.text: Dayton radar approach control issued traffic advisory to TWA 553: uncontrolled VFR traffic ahead and slightly to the right, approximately one mile away, at about the same altitude.
Flight crew of DC-9 acknowledged the traffic advisory from approach control.
The front right side of the DC-9 collided with the left side of the Beechcraft Baron 55 during descent. The DC-9 was at 323 knots at the moment of impact. Both aircraft were destroyed.

safety_changes: Emphasis on improved visual scanning techniques during descent and approach in congested airspace
Enhanced traffic awareness training for flight crews descending into terminal areas

notes: Report verified: McDonnell Douglas DC-9 N1063T and Beechcraft Baron, near Urbana Ohio, March 9, 1967
Limited detail extracted due to brevity - this was a classic See-and-Avoid failure with high descent rate contributing
No CVR transcript available or mentioned in this early accident report
All 26 occupants (12 on DC-9, 14 including pilot and passengers on Baron per collision data) killed
